pageProps.title: Getting Started with the SmartThings API - Environment Setup
pageProps.review: A detailed explanation of the initial setup steps for using the SmartThings API, from issuing a Personal Access Token (PAT) to retrieving a list of registered devices using curl commands.
pageProps.description: A beginner's guide to setting up your environment for the SmartThings API. This post covers generating tokens and making your first API calls.
pageProps.content: ## Getting Started with the SmartThings API - Environment Setup I needed to control devices using the SmartThings API, so I set up the environment. Let's call the API to check the list of devices currently registered in my SmartThings. ### 1. Get a Personal Access Token To use the SmartThings API, you naturally need a Personal Access Token (PAT). This token acts as an authentication key. ### 1. Go to the Personal Access Token page and log in with your Samsung Account Access [https://account.smartthings.com/tokens](https://account.smartthings.com/tokens) and log in with your Samsung Account. ### 2. Name the token, select scopes, and create Give it an easily identifiable name and select the scope of permissions for the token. Security-related permissions should always be granted at the minimum necessary scope. Since I only need device control, I selected only the permissions for Device. ### 3. Save the token Once the token is generated, copy and save it in a safe place. You won't be able to see this token again. ### 2. Make an API Call Now you can call the API using the token. Let's check the device list by making a simple API call with `curl`. Use the token you just saved in YOUR_TOKEN. ```shell { "title": "List all devices using curl" } --- $ curl -X GET "https://api.smartthings.com/v1/devices" -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" ``` If the request is successful, you will receive a JSON response containing the device list. ```json { "title": "Respone from curl" } --- { "items": [ { "deviceId": "xxxxxxxxxxx", "name": "Wireless-Charging-Hub", "label": "SmartThings Station", "manufacturerName": "Samsung Electronics", "presentationId": "XXXXXXXXXXXXXX", "deviceManufacturerCode": "Samsung Electronics", "locationId": "XXXXXXXXXXXXXX", "ownerId": "XXXXXXXXXXXXXX", "roomId": "XXXXXXXXXXXXXX", "deviceTypeId": "Charger", "components": [ { "id": "main", "label": "main", "capabilities": [ { "id": "samsungim.samsungaccount", "version": 1 }, ... ``` ### 3. Make an API Call Using Python I've also written some sample code in Python. ```python { "title": "List all devices using python" } --- import aiohttp import asyncio TOKEN = "xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxx-xxxx" async def main(): headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "Content-Type": "application/json" } url = "https://api.smartthings.com/v1/devices" async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session: async with session.get(url, headers=headers) as response: if response.status == 200: data = await response.json() items = data.get('items', []) print("-" * 30) print(f"total {len(items)}") print("-" * 30) for device in items: name = device.get('label') or device.get('name') device_id = device.get('deviceId') components = device.get('components', []) has_switch = any('switch' in comp.get('capabilities', []) for comp in components) print(f"📱 Device Name: {name}") print(f"🆔 Device ID: {device_id}") print("-" * 30) else: print(f" error: {response.status}") print(await response.text()) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ``` ### 4. Next Steps The environment setup for device control using the SmartThings API is now complete. I plan to try various things by referring to the [SmartThings API documentation](https://developer.smartthings.com/docs/api/public) whenever I have some free time.
